slot.brief: Give three-four statements on components, formation conditions and oxidant character of photochemical smog (vs classical smog); ask which are correct.

stem:
Consider the following statements about smog:
I. Photochemical smog forms in warm, stagnant air under intense sunlight.
II. It involves photolysis of $\text{NO}_2$ and oxidation of volatile organic compounds.
III. $\text{O}_3$ and PAN are oxidants in photochemical smog, unlike the reducing classical smog.
IV. $\text{SO}_2$ and smoke are its principal characteristic components.
Which statements are correct?

verdicts.working: I–III describe photochemical smog; SO₂ and smoke are characteristic of classical smog, so IV is false.

working:
I, II, III: true.\nIV: false; $\text{SO}_2$ and smoke are characteristic of classical smog.

Independent check: I–III describe photochemical smog; SO₂ and smoke are characteristic of classical smog, so IV is false.
solution: Photochemical smog forms in warm, stagnant air under intense sunlight; it involves photolysis of $\text{NO}_2$ and oxidation of $VOCs.\nIts$ oxidants include $\text{O}_3$ and PAN, while $\text{SO}_2$ and smoke characterize classical $smog.\nThus$, statements I, II and III are correct.
